issues.legal_issue: A direction to protect compensation from acquired property extends to tax withheld from that compensation and later refunded, so using the refund without court permission is prima facie a violation of the direction.
material_facts: The court directed that compensation for acquired company land be paid to the court and protected pending further orders.
The payer deducted tax from the compensation and deposited the remainder with the court.
The company later claimed and received a refund based on the tax deduction, then used the refunded money without seeking permission from the court.
The refund was derived from the compensation that the court had directed to be protected.
issues.conclusion: The refund remained part of the compensation covered by the protection order. The company’s use of it without leave was prima facie in violation of that order; claiming the refund itself was not improper.
issues.legal_principle: For a contempt proceeding under the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, a court may consider directions that are explicit or plainly self-evident in the order alleged to have been breached: Sudhir Vasudeva, Chairman and Managing Director, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited v. M. George Ravishekaran, (2014) 3 SCC 373. A tax refund derived from compensation covered by a direction to protect that compensation does not cease to be part of it merely because it passed through the tax authority.

rule.if: company_winding_up_contempt_proceeding and compensation_protection_order and tax_withheld_from_compensation and refund_received and refund_used_without_court_leave

predicates.company_winding_up_contempt_proceeding: A contempt proceeding concerned an alleged breach of a court order in a company winding-up matter.
predicates.compensation_protection_order: The court directed that compensation from acquired company property be paid to the court and protected pending further orders.
predicates.tax_withheld_from_compensation: The payer withheld tax from the compensation and paid the net amount to the court.
predicates.refund_received: The company received a tax refund based on the tax withheld from the compensation.
predicates.refund_used_without_court_leave: The company used the refunded money without obtaining the court’s permission.
predicates.prima_facie_order_violation: The company’s conduct appeared, at a preliminary stage, to breach the court’s direction.

issues.definition: When a company in a winding-up contempt proceeding receives and uses without permission a refund derived from compensation that a court ordered protected, the use is prima facie a violation of that order.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court should not set aside a safeguard securing funds prima facie used contrary to a court order when the safeguard is needed to remedy the consequences of that use.
material_facts: The company used the tax refund derived from the protected compensation without court permission.
A lower court directed the company to secure the amount and restricted operation of its accounts unless it did so.
Some of the refunded money had been placed in a fixed deposit as security for a bank guarantee.
The appellate court vacated the restriction on the company’s bank accounts, and the Supreme Court held that it should not have done so.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court restored a safeguard requiring the company to secure the remaining amount before operating its accounts after the specified date, and directed that the fixed deposit not be withdrawn without leave of the court. The company could apply to the lower court for clarification or modification after securing the required amount.
issues.legal_principle: A court has a duty to issue appropriate directions to remedy or rectify conduct in violation of its orders and may take restitutive measures at any stage of the proceedings: Delhi Development Authority v. Skipper Construction Co. (P) Ltd., (1996) 4 SCC 622. The safeguards in this case were imposed without finally determining the pending contempt proceeding.

rule.if: appeal_from_interim_fund_safeguard and company_winding_up_contempt_proceeding and refund_used_without_court_leave and court_order_protected_compensation and part_of_refund_held_as_security

predicates.appeal_from_interim_fund_safeguard: An appeal challenged an interim direction requiring funds to be secured and restricting operation of company accounts.
predicates.company_winding_up_contempt_proceeding: The underlying matter concerned an alleged breach of a court order in a company winding-up proceeding.
predicates.refund_used_without_court_leave: The company used a refund derived from protected compensation without permission from the court.
predicates.court_order_protected_compensation: The court had directed that compensation from acquired company property be paid to the court and protected pending further orders.
predicates.part_of_refund_held_as_security: Some of the refunded money was held in a fixed deposit as security for a bank guarantee.
predicates.funds_must_be_secured_before_account_ope: The company may not operate its accounts unless it first secures the remaining amount that must be protected.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an interim safeguard after a company has used protected compensation without permission, the remaining amount must be secured before the company operates its accounts.
